newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais to charge Sanyo workers with arson.
newsitem.headline: Thais to charge Sanyo workers with arson.

text.p: Thai prosecutors said on Wednesday they would file charges against 16 employees of Sanyo Universal Electric Plc suspected in the torching of the company's head office and warehouse in December.

A statement from the prosecutor's office said the suspects would be charged with arson, civil disturbance and property destruction on Thursday. The various offences carry maximum penalties of death or life imprisonment.
It said the 16 workers and six colleagues still at large had led a violent protest that caused 546 million baht ($21.2 million) in damage to company property on the outskirts of Bangkok.
"It is a serious and violent crime that damaged the economy and investment sentiment among foreigners, especially the Japanese who were Sanyo Universal's partners," it said.
Sanyo Electric Co of Japan owns about 30 percent of Sanyo Universal Electric Plc.
The prosecutor's statement said the office would also seek court permission to issue arrest warrants of up to 20 years for the six suspects who had eluded police arrests.
"The prosecutor's office would pursue the case in order to fully enforce Thai laws with an aim of restoring the foreign investment climate," it said.

It said police had witnesses, pictures and video tapes implicating the suspects of leading the torching of the Sanyo complex, which stored a large inventory of refrigerators, cooling unit compressors and television sets.

The suspects led about 2,000 Sanyo Universal staff and workers in a protest rally to press their demand for year-end bonuses worth 5.75 months of their salaries. The company had offered an average bonus of three months salary.
